clue.text: Kilts set in motion as they get sent flying in alleys

definitions.text: they get sent flying in alleys

indicators.note: something in motion is moving about, so the letters before it are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: Kilts swirl as Scottish dancers fling themselves about in narrow lanes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set in motion' reads as one phrase, but 'set' belongs to the letters being shuffled. A skittle alley is the British lane in which the game of skittles, a cousin of ninepins, is played.
explanation.definitionFit: Skittles are the wooden pins that a thrown ball knocks over in a skittle alley.

clue.text: Dignified meeting of lovers under superbly elegant covers

indicators.note: covers sit on top of things, so only the leading letters of the words are kept
in a down entry, one part placed under another simply follows it

blocks.note: the opening letters of the two words
a romantic meeting is a date

explanation.surface: A refined lovers' tryst taking place beneath beautiful bedclothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covers' looks like bedding the lovers lie under, but it asks for the tops of the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedate describes calm, composed and decorous behaviour, close in sense to dignified.

clue.text: Protect and toughen around top of skull

indicators.note: one thing going round another encloses it
the top of a word in a down clue is its opening letter

blocks.note: to inure is to harden or accustom to hardship

explanation.surface: Advice to shield and harden the head, like a helmet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top of' in a down clue means the first letter, which sits snugly inside the synonym for toughen.
explanation.definitionFit: To insure something is to safeguard it against loss, a way to protect it financially.

clue.text: Credit the one who portrayed F Gump?

blocks.note: writing Forrest as F invites the same shortening of the actor's first name, Tom
Tom Hanks played Forrest Gump in the 1994 film

explanation.surface: Give due credit to the actor behind Forrest Gump.
explanation.walkthrough: The abbreviated 'F Gump' is the hint: shorten the actor the same way, Tom to T, and the name runs on into one word.
explanation.definitionFit: To credit someone for something is to give them thanks or acknowledgement for it.

clue.text: Sir Bradley cycled around those who got there first

indicators.note: riding round and round churns things up, so the letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: Sir Bradley Wiggins, the British Tour de France winner, lapping the riders who finished ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: The famous cyclist makes 'cycled' look literal, but the knight's name and title supply the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Early birds are people who arrive or act before others, from the proverb about catching the worm.

clue.text: Come across an equal in audition

indicators.note: an audition is a hearing, so the answer is taken from what is heard

blocks.note: a peer is someone of equal standing

explanation.surface: Meeting a fellow performer of the same level at a casting session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come across' looks like 'meet', but here it means to seem or show oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: To come across as something is to appear that way, the phrasal verb meaning seem.

clue.text: By hacking, clear top of the chest

indicators.note: hacking chops things up, so the letters are broken and reassembled

explanation.surface: Coughing hard to clear the upper airways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hacking' suggests a hacking cough and 'chest' completes the picture, but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Pectoral is the adjective for things relating to the breast or thorax, as in pectoral muscles.

clue.text: The setter, we hear, is able to outwardly decry something aesthetically pleasing

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the word is chosen by its sound
the outward part of a word is its two ends, so only those are kept

blocks.note: a setter calls themselves I or me

explanation.surface: The setter can find fault with something attractive on the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is able to' is a plain synonym chunk, not a link. Crossword setters often refer to themselves as 'the setter', meaning I.
explanation.definitionFit: Eye candy is slang for something visually attractive but of little substance.

clue.text: Listener in tears hits back

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside it

blocks.note: the ear is the organ that listens

explanation.surface: Someone crying who then retaliates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tears' reads as weeping but is the verb, as in tears apart. 'Hits back' is not retaliation but a car hitting the back of another.
explanation.definitionFit: To rear-end a vehicle is to crash into its back, so a driver who rear-ends another strikes its rear.

clue.text: Abandons all hope in a spider's web

indicators.note: a web is a tangle, so these letters are woven into a different order

blocks.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A fly caught in a spider's web gives up hope.
explanation.walkthrough: The web is the trap in the picture, but it is the instruction to tangle the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To despair is to lose or give up every expectation that things will improve.

clue.text: Clears out the white of the eye

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or wrong, so the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Something that cleans out the white part of the eye, like eye drops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clears out' looks like one phrasal verb; split it and 'out' is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The sclera is the tough opaque outer coat of the eyeball, seen as its white part.

clue.text: Christmas dinners have no starter for old prison officers

indicators.note: to have something is to hold it, so one piece is held inside another
the starter of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: turkey is the traditional British Christmas dinner

explanation.surface: Prison guards of old went without a first course at Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Have no starter' looks like a missing first course, or a deletion; instead the start of 'no' goes inside the birds.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnkey was a jailer, the keeper of the keys who locked and unlocked cells.

clue.text: What should be taken if wise man turns up after party?

indicators.note: coming after places one piece behind the other in the order

blocks.note: a sage is a wise man

explanation.surface: Wondering what remedy to take when a wise guest shows up after a party.
explanation.walkthrough: The question reads like a hangover cure; 'turns up' only means arrives, and the wise man follows the party.
explanation.definitionFit: A dosage is the measured amount of a medicine prescribed to be swallowed at a time.

clue.text: Messenger is absorbed by game that's fast

indicators.note: whatever is absorbed is taken inside something else

blocks.note: angel comes from the Greek for messenger

explanation.surface: A courier gets engrossed in a quick-fire game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' suggests speed, as in a fast game, but here it means fixed, as in holding fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Fast can mean firmly fixed or steadfast, and changeless describes something constant that never varies.

clue.text: Intoxicated and given to be overbearing

explanation.surface: Someone drunk and inclined to be domineering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given to' looks like 'prone to', but 'given' is a piece on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: High-handed behaviour is imperious and arrogant, ignoring others' views, which is what overbearing means.

clue.text: Element found in a cholesterol-reducing drug and vitamin

blocks.note: statins are drugs that lower cholesterol

explanation.surface: A chemical element present in a heart medicine and a vitamin supplement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found in' sounds like an instruction to look inside the words, but it only joins the definition to the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Astatine is a rare radioactive halogen, number 85 in the periodic table.

clue.text: They learn choral arrangement in two seconds

indicators.note: a musical arrangement reworks material, so the letters are reordered
being in something means sitting inside it

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second, twice

explanation.surface: Singers pick up a choir piece in no time at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Choral arrangement' reads as a piece of music, but 'arrangement' tells you to reorder the letters, which then sit between the two S's.
explanation.definitionFit: Scholars are students or learned people, those who study and acquire knowledge.

clue.text: Pessimistic, for example, in domestic surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings enclose whatever is in their midst

blocks.note: e.g. is the abbreviation for 'for example'
domestic in the sense of home-grown, not foreign

explanation.surface: Someone feeling gloomy, perhaps, at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Domestic' suggests the household, but it means home-grown, as in domestic produce.
explanation.definitionFit: A negative person expects the worst, which is what being pessimistic means.

clue.text: Gaining ranking after draw is announced

indicators.note: coming after places one piece behind the other in the order
what is announced is spoken aloud, so the answer is chosen by sound

blocks.note: to draw on a straw is to suck
seeding ranks players in a tournament draw

explanation.surface: A player moving up the rankings once the tournament draw is made public.
explanation.walkthrough: The tennis picture makes 'draw' the tournament draw, but it means suck. Said together, 'suck seeding' gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Succeeding means achieving one's aim, so it can stand for gaining success or ground.

clue.text: Greatest duty is essentially to lead the largest number

indicators.note: the essence of something is its core, so only the middle letters are kept
in a down clue, leading puts one piece above, and so before, the other

blocks.note: most is the largest number or amount

explanation.surface: A utilitarian maxim: the highest obligation is to serve the greatest number.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes 'the greatest good of the greatest number'.
explanation.definitionFit: Utmost means of the highest degree or extreme, as in the utmost importance.

clue.text: Old cronies abandoned leader and fell into disarray

indicators.note: giving up its leader means the word loses its first letter
disarray is disorder, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: the word without its first letter

explanation.surface: A gang of old friends ditched their boss and descended into chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old cronies' looks like one phrase, but 'Old' is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Senior describes someone older or advanced in years, as in senior citizens.

clue.text: Characters in Macbeth? Nice and traditional

indicators.note: characters are letters, and those inside the following words make up the solution

blocks.note: running across the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: Asking whether Shakespeare's Macbeth characters are pleasant and old-fashioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters in Macbeth' wants to be the witches or Banquo; it means the letters inside the words.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethnic is used of folk customs, dress and food belonging to a particular cultural heritage.

clue.text: In the morning, speaking with no sense of right or wrong

definitions.text: with no sense of right or wrong

explanation.surface: Someone talking at dawn without any moral compass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like it may place one piece inside another, but 'In the morning' is the whole of AM.
explanation.definitionFit: Amoral means lacking moral standards altogether, unconcerned with ethics rather than opposed to them.

clue.text: Test size ingredients are the most piquant

indicators.note: ingredients are mixed together in a recipe, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A trial batch of spices turns out to be the tangiest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ingredients' sits naturally in a cooking scene but tells you to mix the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Zesty food is lively and tangy in flavour, so the zestiest is the sharpest and spiciest.

clue.text: Shelled facility is twisted and sloping

indicators.note: a shelled nut has lost its outer casing, so the outside letters go
something twisted is bent out of shape, so the letters change order

blocks.note: the word without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A bombed building left bent and leaning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shelled' suggests an artillery attack, which fits the twisted building, but it means stripped of its shell.
explanation.definitionFit: Italic type leans to the right, so slanting letters are described as italic.

clue.text: Anaesthetised foot has feeling but it's lowering

indicators.note: the foot of a word is its end, so only its last letter is kept

explanation.surface: A numbed foot still has sensation, but it is sinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anaesthetised foot' reads as a numb limb; 'foot' is the selector, pointing at the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A demotion lowers someone in rank or status, a reduction in position.

clue.text: Realise rubbish left out is not so problematic

indicators.note: whatever is out has been excluded, so a letter is dropped from the word
as a verb or adjective rubbish suggests a wrecked state, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left, the letter removed

explanation.surface: Discovering that leaving the bins out makes things less of a headache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubbish left out' looks like bin bags at the kerb; 'left' is L and the letter to remove.
explanation.definitionFit: Easier is the comparative of easy, meaning less difficult or troublesome.

clue.text: Enigmatic sweetheart gets drunk with Ernie's other half

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, so only the middle letter is kept

blocks.note: Eric Morecambe was Ernie Wise's partner in the British comedy double act Morecambe and Wise

explanation.surface: A mysterious lover gets tipsy alongside Ernie's spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweetheart' reads as a lover, but it splits into 'sweet' and its heart. 'Other half' suggests a wife; it is the other half of a famous comedy duo.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric knowledge is obscure and understood only by a few, so it can be called mysterious or puzzling.
